items.detail: Four kitchen-depth cases are derived from the 12.5-ft casework run, 13-ft end of the current stool proxy, 13.5-ft M178 cross-section and 14-ft M178 depth.
Each nominal five-foot opening lies wholly within its translated porch face, and the generated porch wall segments move with that opening.
Every found route reports a 3-in proxy reserve to the original owner-protected west-A boundary.
M186, M178, M192, room/porch spec, selected-D, bath-window source, M207 pantry study and owner area/open-connection/A-protection decisions are fingerprinted.
A 3-in analytical search reserve is held constant; it is not an M-06 design/code requirement.
Among these samples, 12.5 ft flags 6 in of stool-proxy overhang; 13 ft just contains the existing stool proxy with zero margin.
Selected-D remains at the protected source hash.
The M178 8 x 4 ft island is retained in the full-shell route engine.
Owner-protected A and unassigned B remain clear of moved dining/porch blocks; route search keeps both as obstacles.
All table/chair bodies and the four 36-in use-zone proxies fit each translated 11 x 10 ft dining study block.
The translated dining and 12 x 10 ft porch footprints stay inside the 40 x 42 ft shell test.
Every generated M186 route run passes its source and finite-grid contract checks.
Even a path with positive geometric gap remains an unselected schematic candidate.
